AccountEvent.description: One line of *Sign-ins and changes*: who, what, when, and by whom for a change. Never a password or text.
AccountEvent.title: AccountEvent

AdminCase.description:
A case as the administrator's list shows it (stage 4): with its manager's name and how many
members it has. Nothing from inside the case.
AdminCase.title: AdminCase

AnswerContent.description:
What rebuilds the Word file (the chat UI's own data): the question, the answer as written, its
sources and checks, and the file names of the sources as they were.
AnswerContent.title: AnswerContent

AnswerIn.description:
Body of ``POST …/runs/{run}/answer``: a person's answer to the step the run is waiting on.
For an ``ask``: ``facts`` (a value per fact asked; empty: not known yet). For a ``request``:
nothing (the documents are in the case; the runtime counts them) or ``none: true`` (there is no
such document, when the step allows it). ``text`` is what the person wrote, if anything: the thread keeps the
values given (``answers``) and the screen words them in each reader's language.
AnswerIn.title: AnswerIn

BackendStatus.description: State of the model server as seen from the gateway.
BackendStatus.title: BackendStatus

BackupFailure.description: Why the last backup failed: a message of the registry, as the backup service wrote it (docs/design/messages.md).
BackupFailure.title: BackupFailure

BackupRequest.description:
What the administrator asks the backup service for. ``settings``: the target (a USB disk by the id the
service lists, or a share with its address, user and password), the retention, the hour and, only with a
new recovery key, its public half. ``keep_password``: a share's password left empty keeps the saved one.
BackupRequest.title: BackupRequest

BackupSettings.description: Where, when and how long, as saved (``backups.json``). Never the share's password: only whether one is kept.
BackupSettings.title: BackupSettings

BackupStatus.description:
``available``: the appliance has a backup service that has run at least once. ``configured``: a
target is set (the web setup's Backups step). The rest only when known.
BackupStatus.title: BackupStatus

Calculation.description:
A calculation in a grounded answer, computed exactly by the server (``suveryn_harness.calc``).

The model only chooses the figures; the result is never the model's own arithmetic.
``figures_not_in_sources`` lists figures that don't appear (as whole numbers) in the passages
the answer cites, which a reader should check. ``result`` is None (and ``error`` says why) if it couldn't be computed.
Calculation.title: Calculation

Case.description:
A case as the API returns it. ``my_role`` is the caller's: a member's role, ``reader`` for a
non-member in an office-wide appliance, None for an administrator who only sees it exists.
Case.title: Case

CaseEvent.description: One line of a case's access log: who, when, what (never document text).
CaseEvent.title: CaseEvent

CaseIn.description: Body of ``POST /v1/cases``: the office's file number, a name and the type.
CaseIn.title: CaseIn

CaseOverview.description:
A case as the Cases overview shows it (docs/design/chat-ui.md §4): with its members (the
manager first) and its last activity, who and when, from the access log. For an administrator who
isn't a member, no members: only that the case exists.
CaseOverview.title: CaseOverview

CaseTypeOut.description:
A case type an appliance offers (``GET /v1/case-types``, suveryn-tracker#229): its id, the pack that
brings it (core's reference content or an installed pack) and its word per language, which the screen shows.
CaseTypeOut.title: CaseTypeOut

CaseUpdate.description: Body of ``PATCH /v1/cases/{id}``: what a manager may change. Fields left out stay as they are.
CaseUpdate.title: CaseUpdate

ChatMessage.description: One turn of the conversation, in OpenAI chat format.
ChatMessage.title: ChatMessage

ChatRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /v1/chat``.

Limits are deliberately bounded: ``max_tokens`` up to 8192 keeps one request from occupying
the GPU for minutes, and ``temperature`` defaults to 0 because notarial answers should be
reproducible rather than creative. The last message must be the user's question; the
conversation is limited to 200 messages, each message to 100,000 characters, and all of them
together to ``MAX_TOTAL_CHARS``.
ChatRequest.title: ChatRequest

ChatResponse.description:
A complete answer. Returned as JSON, or as the final ``done`` event of a stream.

``model`` is the model file llama-server reports (e.g. ``Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf``), so a
reviewer can always tell which model produced an answer.

Citation contract: in a grounded answer, the marker ``[n]`` in ``answer`` refers to
``citations[n - 1]``. ``citations`` holds every passage the model was given, in that order;
a passage the answer never cites is still listed, so clients show only the cited ones.
ChatResponse.title: ChatResponse

CheckOut.description:
One check step's result as last computed (``suveryn_harness.checks``): the rule holds, fails (both
sides as computed, for the notary) or is open (values it needs are missing or can't be read).
CheckOut.title: CheckOut

Citation.description: A passage the answer relies on. ``source`` is null when the passage can't be traced to a document.

context.description: The passage with the sentences around it on its page; null on a short page, a spreadsheet or a scan without text around it

source.description: null means unsourced; show as unverified

text.description: The passage or claim that is being cited
text.title: Text

Citation.title: Citation

CitationIssue.description:
A fact in a cited claim that the cited passage doesn't contain (suveryn-tracker#11).

``marker`` is the 0-based occurrence of the marker in ``answer``, counting only markers that refer
to an existing citation, in text order; ``n`` is its number. ``found_in`` lists other passages that
do contain ``item``; ``written_as`` is how a passage spells a name the answer spells differently.
CitationIssue.title: CitationIssue

ConfirmIn.description:
Body of ``PUT …/runs/{run}/facts``: every fact's confirmed value (a correction, the value as
read, or empty). The summary is written in the run's language, the thread's.
ConfirmIn.title: ConfirmIn

Conversation.description:
Body of ``GET /v1/conversations/{id}``: each turn as the UI saved it, with ``seq``, ``by`` and
``at`` (and a playbook's ``step_id``) from its row.
Conversation.title: Conversation

ConversationIn.description: Body of ``PUT /v1/conversations/{id}``: the whole conversation, replacing what was stored.
ConversationIn.title: ConversationIn

Deletion.description: What deleting an account removes (its own space) and what stays with its cases.
Deletion.title: Deletion

FactAlternative.description:
A later document's reading that differs from what a person confirmed (or answered): shown beside it until a
person chooses at the checkpoint; the confirmed value stands meanwhile (decision of 10 November 2026).
FactAlternative.title: FactAlternative

FactCitation.description: A passage a fact was read from: enough to show it later, also after the document is deleted.
FactCitation.title: FactCitation

FactIn.description:
Body of ``PUT …/runs/{run}/facts/{fact}``: a value from a playbook's card, *Adjust* or *Fill in*
(the value unchanged: the person checked it).
FactIn.title: FactIn

HandoverIn.description: Body of ``POST /v1/cases/{id}/handover``: the member (or colleague) who takes the case over.
HandoverIn.title: HandoverIn

InvalidPart.description: Where a request wasn't valid and why, for developers: never the value sent.
InvalidPart.title: InvalidPart

KeepIn.description:
Body of ``POST /v1/cases/{id}/keep``: mark the case kept (never deleted by the period) or
not, or extend its deletion by one period.
KeepIn.title: KeepIn

KeyTest.description: The last key test: whether the key opened the newest backup and every part was there.
KeyTest.title: KeyTest

LateIn.title: LateIn

Me.description: The signed-in user, for the UI.
Me.title: Me

Measured.description: What a browser measured: the appliance's clock minus its own, and the round trip it measured it in.
Measured.title: Measured

Member.description: One member of a case, as the API lists it (the name as it was when they were added).
Member.title: Member

Message.description: A message as it travels inside an answer: a code of the registry, its kind and its values.
Message.title: Message

ModelInfo.description: An installed model, as listed by ``GET /v1/models``.
ModelInfo.title: ModelInfo

MoveIn.description: Body of ``POST /v1/conversations/{id}/move``: the case a personal conversation moves into.
MoveIn.title: MoveIn

PassageContext.description:
The text around a cited passage on the same page (board G11): ``text`` holds the passage itself at
``[start, end)``, with a few sentences before and after it, for the source panel to dim around it.
PassageContext.title: PassageContext

Person.description: One account, as the API lists it.
Person.title: Person

PlaybookOut.description:
One playbook that fits a case (``GET /v1/cases/{id}/playbooks``), or one of all of them for the
administrator (``GET /v1/admin/playbooks``, with ``active``).
PlaybookOut.title: PlaybookOut

PlaybookWords.description: A playbook's words in one language (``suveryn_playbooks.Wording``).
PlaybookWords.title: PlaybookWords

ProblemDetails.description: What the gateway answers instead of the answer asked for (RFC 9457): the standard members, and the message's.
ProblemDetails.title: ProblemDetails

Rates-Input.description: Notional cost per million tokens, as on a comparable cloud API (admin-editable).
Rates-Input.title: Rates

Rates-Output.description: Notional cost per million tokens, as on a comparable cloud API (admin-editable).
Rates-Output.title: Rates

RenameIn.description: Body of ``PATCH /v1/conversations/{id}``: a title the owner chose, kept over later saves.
RenameIn.title: RenameIn

RequestAnswer.description:
The backup service's answer: ``ok``; when it isn't, why, as messages of the registry (``failure`` for the whole
request, ``fields`` per field); the USB disks; whether the recovery key changed. ``pending`` until it has answered.
RequestAnswer.title: RequestAnswer

SaveAnswerIn.description: Body of ``POST /v1/cases/{id}/documents``: an answer saved to the case (docs/design/chat-ui.md §5).
SaveAnswerIn.title: SaveAnswerIn

SavedCitation.description: A source of the saved answer, as the chat shows it; checked so a deleted document can be taken out.
SavedCitation.title: SavedCitation

SavedTurn.description: One turn as the UI saves it. Only the role is checked; the other fields are the UI's own.
SavedTurn.title: SavedTurn

SayIn.description:
Body of ``POST …/runs/{run}/say``: what a person writes in the run's conversation (the founder, 30
October 2026: a playbook is a conversation). At a ``request``: the documents just added
(``documents``, ids in the case). At an ``ask``: an answer in words, mapped to the facts asked, or
``unknown`` (the quick reply "Not known yet"). At the checkpoint: a correction in words.
SayIn.title: SayIn

SettingsIn.description: Body of ``PUT /v1/admin/cases/settings``: what to change; a field left out stays.
SettingsIn.title: SettingsIn

SettingsOut.description: The office's case settings as they apply now (``GET /v1/admin/cases/settings``).
SettingsOut.title: SettingsOut

SettingsPreview.description: What a change in Settings would do now, for its confirmation (``GET /v1/admin/cases/settings/preview``).
SettingsPreview.title: SettingsPreview

SourceRef.description: Where a cited passage comes from: a stored document, and a position inside it.

location.description: Finer position, e.g. 'p. 3-4 · Article 2 - Price', 'Article 2 › Price' or 'Prices!A2:D31'
location.title: Location

page.description: 1-based page number in the source document
page.title: Page

SourceRef.title: SourceRef

StartIn.description:
Body of ``POST /v1/cases/{id}/playbooks/{playbook}/runs``: which documents to read (none: all
the case's uploaded documents, at the time the read step runs) and the thread's language.
StartIn.title: StartIn

StoreStatus.description:
State of a database-backed feature (saved conversations, token usage): "ready", "failed"
(database unreachable) or "unavailable" (no database configured).
StoreStatus.title: StoreStatus

SupportSpan.description:
What the source card marks for one citation marker (suveryn-tracker#25; ``marking.support_spans``).

``marker`` is the marker's 0-based occurrence among the answer's valid markers, as ``CitationIssue``
counts them; ``n`` its number. ``ranges`` are the sentences of ``citations[n - 1].text`` the claim
rests on, and ``facts`` what to mark strongly: the claim's facts and names, however the passage writes
them. Both are [start, end) offsets in UTF-16 code units, as the browser counts a string.
SupportSpan.title: SupportSpan

Temporary.description: A temporary password to pass on, shown once: where to sign in, and with what.
Temporary.title: Temporary

Turn.description: One line of a thread, as ``turns`` holds it.
Turn.title: Turn

Usage.description: Token counts reported by the model server, for capacity monitoring (no content).
Usage.title: Usage

UsageReport.description: Usage between ``start`` and ``end``: totals, a series in ``step`` buckets (local time), per kind.
UsageReport.title: UsageReport

suveryn_api_gateway__cases__PinIn.description: Body of ``PUT /v1/cases/{id}/pin``: whether the caller pins the case in their sidebar.
suveryn_api_gateway__cases__PinIn.title: PinIn

post.description: End the session; ``logout_url`` ends the Keycloak session too (the UI navigates there).

get.description: The signed-in user (username and display name), or 401.

Report whether the model server is ready (and which model it serves) and whether documents work.

200 when the model server is ready; 503 while it loads, fails or can't be reached. The
``documents`` part doesn't affect the status code: chat works without it. Public (no sign-in),
so it gives states only: no internal addresses or error texts (those are in the server log).
The last backup and the last failure, as the appliance's backup service recorded them.

post.description:
Test the recovery key: the request body is the key file as the web setup downloaded it. The backup
service checks that it opens the newest backup and that every part is there, restores nothing and
deletes the key; GET /v1/admin/backups then shows the result (``key_test``).

409.description: A test is already running

post.description:
Ask the backup service: ``run`` (back up now), ``disks`` (the USB disks connected now), ``test-share``
(sign in to the share and write a test file) or ``settings`` (save the target, retention, hour and a new
recovery key). The answer comes at ``GET /v1/admin/backups/requests/{id}``. The password is never logged
and never comes back.

409.description: The last request is still being handled

get.description: The backup service's answer to a request, or ``pending`` while it is acting on it.

Administrators: every case on the appliance, open ones first, with who manages it and how
many members it has; nothing from inside a case. For handing cases over before an account
goes (decision 6), and for seeing what is closed and due.

Administrators: the office's settings as they apply now: the default access of a new case,
how long closed cases are kept, and how long saved conversations are kept (the data lifecycle,
suveryn-tracker#31). As provisioned, until changed here.

put.description:
Administrators: change the default access (``office`` or ``members``), the keep period of
closed cases and the keep period of saved conversations (each ``6m``, ``1y``, ``5y`` or ``manual``).
Takes effect at once for new cases and for cases closed from now on; a case already closed keeps
its date (extend or keep it from the case). The conversations period applies to every saved
conversation from its last change: shortening it hides the older ones from lists at once and deletes them when it is saved (and by the hourly sweep).

Opening the default access to the office applies to new cases (``apply_to: new``: the existing ones
stay with their members, restricted, and a manager can open one) or to all of them (``all``: every case,
restricted ones too, each with a line in its access log). Closing it to the members applies to every
case that follows the default. Strictly confidential cases never change: their members decide.

get.description:
Administrators: what saving these settings would do now, for the confirmation in Settings: how many
cases become visible to everyone in the office or to their members only, and how many saved
conversations a shorter keep period deletes. Counts only.

post.description:
Administrators: set the appliance's clock to this PC's time, by the difference just measured (Status, after a
confirmation that shows both times). The answer comes at ``GET /v1/admin/clock/{id}``.

409.description: Conflict

get.description: The appliance's answer to setting its clock, or ``pending`` while it acts on it.

Every installed playbook with its case types and whether it is switched on (an administrator's
list; docs/design/admin.md).

put.description:
Switch a playbook on or off for the whole office: off, it leaves every case's menu and can't
be started; runs already made stay.

get.description: Is everything working? The six checks, the latest at most a quarter of a minute old.
Administrators: the office's token usage, per user and in total, with a notional cloud cost.
Administrators: the rates the notional cost uses, per million input and output tokens.

put.description: Administrators: change the rates (e.g. to a cloud model the office would otherwise use).

get.description: Every person's account: name, e-mail, administrator or not, on or off, last sign-in.

post.description:
A new account, with a temporary password to pass on (shown once). The person signs in with the e-mail
address, then chooses a password, and sets up two-step sign-in when the office requires it (Settings).

409.description: The e-mail address has an account

get.description:
*Sign-ins and changes*, newest first: Keycloak's sign-in events and its admin events on accounts, kept 180
days, each change with the administrator who made it. Names and actions only.

delete.description:
Delete an account (decision, 29 October). Only one that is switched off, so its cases are handed over already.
Its own space goes with it: its documents outside a case, the conversations nobody else can read, its picture,
its pins. What it did in its cases stays with them under its name: documents it added, conversations it
shared, the access log. Then the account itself, in Keycloak. Usage keeps its counts. Repeatable: a step
that failed is done again.

409.description: Your own account, one that is on, or one that manages cases

put.description: Make someone an administrator, or remove the rights; never the last administrator's.

409.description: The last administrator

get.description: What deleting this account would remove, for the confirmation: counts only.

409.description: Your own account, one that is on, or one that manages cases

put.description:
Switch an account off, or on again. Off: not your own, not the last administrator, and only once every
case it manages has a new manager.

409.description: Your own account, the last administrator, or the account still manages cases

post.description: A new temporary password: the current one stops working.
Signed out on every device; they can sign in again straight away.

The authenticator app removed (a lost phone): the person sets it up again at the next sign-in when the office
requires two-step sign-in, and may otherwise.

get.description:
The case types this appliance offers, in order: core's reference content's, then each installed pack's
(suveryn-tracker#229). A type without a playbook is offered too; a stored case keeps its type when the
type's pack is gone.

The cases the caller may see: open ones first, most recently active first. Closed cases
only with ``closed=true``. ``my_role`` is the caller's role in each.

post.description:
Open a new case. The caller becomes its manager and first member.
The reference is the office's own file number, unique on this appliance; never put a client's
name in it or the name. The type is one this appliance offers (``GET /v1/case-types``).

409.description: A case with this reference exists

422.description: A case type this appliance doesn't offer

get.description:
Every case the caller may see, open and closed, as the Cases overview shows them
(docs/design/chat-ui.md §4): each with its members (the manager first, with their pictures'
ETags) and its last activity, who and when. An administrator who isn't a member sees no members.

delete.description:
Delete a case with its documents and conversations (its manager only). Closing and the
keep period (docs/design/cases.md, stage 3) are the office's way; this is for a case opened
by mistake. See ``Store.delete_document`` for what deletion does and doesn't guarantee.

503.description: A store the case is in can't be reached: nothing was deleted

get.description: One case the caller may see.

patch.description:
Change a case's reference, name, type, access or strictly confidential label (its
manager only). Turning the label on restricts the access and unshares the case's conversations.
A new type is one this appliance offers; a case whose stored type it no longer offers keeps it, and
its other fields still change.

403.description: Not the case's manager, or the case is closed

409.description: A case with this reference exists, or the access can't be opened while strictly confidential

422.description: A case type this appliance doesn't offer

post.description:
Close the case (its manager only): read-only from now, reopenable while it is kept, and
deleted after the office's keep period (``SUVERYN_CASES_KEEP``; with ``manual``, kept until
deleted by hand). ``keep_until`` says when.

409.description: Already closed

post.description:
Save an answer to its case, as a document with origin ``answer`` (docs/design/chat-ui.md §5): a
contributor's right in an open case. Never a source (cases.md decision 7); listed, searchable,
deleted with the case. Its file is rebuilt by the chat from ``content`` (``GET .../content``).
Saving the same message again gives the document already saved. Logged as ``answer_saved``.

200.description: This answer was saved before: that document

403.description: Not a contributor, or the case is closed

get.description:
The case's access log, newest first: who did what, when (decision 15). For its manager
and the administrators; kept 180 days, as the sign-in events.

403.description: Neither the case's manager nor an administrator

post.description:
Make another colleague the case's manager: the current manager may, and an administrator
(decision 6: an account can't go while it manages a case). The previous manager stays on as
a contributor.

403.description: Neither the case's manager nor an administrator

post.description:
On a closed case: ``{"keep": true}`` marks it kept (never deleted by the period), ``{"keep":
false}`` plans its deletion one period from now again, ``{"extend": true}`` moves its
deletion one period later. The manager's and the administrators' right (decision 11).

403.description: Neither the case's manager nor an administrator

409.description: Not closed

get.description: The case's members and their roles, the manager first (anyone who may read the case).

delete.description:
Take a member out of the case (the manager's right). The manager can't be removed: hand
the case over first.

403.description: Not the case's manager, or the case is closed

404.description: Unknown case or not a member

put.description:
Add a colleague to the case as a reader or contributor, or change a member's role (the
manager's right). The colleague must be one of the office's accounts. To make someone the
manager, hand the case over (``POST .../handover``).

403.description: Not the case's manager, or the case is closed

422.description: The manager's role is changed by handing over

put.description:
Pin or unpin the case in the caller's own sidebar (docs/design/chat-ui.md): anyone who may
read it; per user, never shared, not in the access log.

get.description:
The playbooks that fit this case's type and are switched on, each with whether it is covered
by the appliance's support agreement (``covered`` false: it runs, with a warning; never a block).
The case's runs, newest first (a reader's right).
One run: where it is, its thread, its facts as read and as confirmed with the passages they came from.

post.description:
A contributor answers the step the run waits on. An ``ask``: ``facts`` with a value per fact
(empty: still unknown; the checkpoint can fill it). A ``request``: the documents are in the case
now, or ``none`` when the step allows that. The answer is written in the thread and the run walks on.

409.description: The run isn't waiting on that step

post.description:
The run should not have happened: every fact it established, confirmed or not, is superseded
(kept in the record, no longer the case's), its product is marked withdrawn (never deleted), and
the case shows no result from it.

403.description: Not the starter or the manager

409.description: Already ended

post.description:
Documents that came after their request was answered: the bank certificate a week after the plan (decision of
10 November 2026). They are recorded as that request's, the reads aimed at it are read again, and the checkpoint
follows again; a confirmed run is reopened, its summary out of date until confirmed again. A reading that differs
from a confirmed value waits beside it for a person to choose. While the request itself is the step the run waits
on, it is answered as usual (``/say``, ``/answer``).

404.description: Unknown document, or no such request in this playbook

409.description: The run can't take a document now, or the request doesn't apply

put.description:
The checkpoint (a contributor's right; the case manager's when the step says ``by: manager``): every
fact's confirmed value, a correction or empty, and entries added to a list. The run then walks on: the
summary is stored in the case as a document with origin ``playbook``.

409.description: The run isn't waiting at its checkpoint, or its facts changed since ``seen``

put.description:
A value from a playbook's card at the checkpoint (handover of 31 October 2026): *Adjust* or *Fill
in*. A new version from this person, as a correction in words is; changed, the playbook says so in
the thread. The same value as before says the person checked it: a version from them, no turn. The
run stays at the checkpoint; confirming is a separate act.

409.description: The run isn't waiting at its checkpoint

post.description:
Keep everything and wait (anyone who contributes to the case). A run that is reading can't be
paused mid-call; pause it when it waits.

409.description: Not waiting
Not paused
The run isn't waiting on a person

503.description: The model isn't available to read an answer in words

post.description:
End early, keeping what was achieved: confirmed facts stay the case's; proposed ones go;
a product made so far stays as a document. A new run asks again: the confirmed facts aren't offered to it yet.

403.description: Not the starter or the manager

409.description: Already ended

post.description:
Start a run (a contributor's right, in an open case) and walk it to its first wait: a
request for documents, or straight into reading when the case has them and the routine starts
there. ``document_ids`` narrows what the read step reads (none: every uploaded document, at the
time it reads). Answers with the run; poll it, or answer what it asks.

403.description: Not a contributor, or the case is closed

404.description: No such case, playbook or document

409.description: A run of this playbook is already going in this case

post.description: Reopen a closed case (its manager only): open again, no deletion planned.

409.description: Not closed

post.description:
Answer a conversation. With ``document_ids``, ground the answer in those documents.

Grounded answers cite passages as [n], where [n] is ``citations[n-1]``. Without
``document_ids`` the answer is unsourced (``citations: []``) and must be shown as unverified.

200.description: With stream=true: SSE events `status` ({step, ...}), for a grounded answer `sources` ({citations}), with `thinking` true and a model that can think `thinking` ({text}, its reasoning), `delta` ({text}), then `done` (a full ChatResponse) or `error` ({kind, code, params}, a code of the registry, and an English detail). Closing the connection stops the answer: the model stops writing.

404.description: A document id doesn't exist or belongs to another user

422.description: Invalid request, e.g. a malformed document id

503.description: Model backend unreachable or returned an error, or grounded answer requested but document search is unavailable

get.description: The appliance's clock, for a signed-in browser to measure the difference with its own.

post.description:
A signed-in browser's measurement. The newest per account counts for a day; when they agree the
appliance is asked to nudge its clock (``clock.Clock.report``).

delete.description: Delete all of the caller's conversations (the "Delete history" choice when signing out).

get.description:
The caller's saved conversations in their personal space, or in the case ``case`` their own
and the ones its members shared (``shared``, ``owner``), most recently changed first (titles
and dates, no content). With ``all``: every one of their own, across the cases they may read
and their personal space (the sidebar's list, docs/design/chat-ui.md).

delete.description: Delete one of the caller's conversations. A playbook run's goes with its case: stop or cancel the run.

404.description: Not the caller's conversation, or a playbook run's (it goes with its case)

get.description:
One of the caller's conversations with all its turns, or one shared with a case the caller
may read (read-only for them: saving it answers 404).

404.description: Unknown, expired or another user's conversation

patch.description:
Rename one of the caller's conversations (docs/design/chat-ui.md §4). The title is kept over
later saves, which otherwise name a conversation after its first question.

put.description:
Save the whole conversation under an id the client chose (a UUID): its turns' rows are brought in
line with the body's. ``case_id`` puts a new conversation in that case (the caller must be able to
read it); a saved conversation stays where it was first saved. A playbook run's conversation is
written by the server, never saved over: 404.

404.description: The id belongs to another user's conversation

post.description:
Move one of the caller's personal conversations into a case they contribute to (§4). It isn't
shared, loses its own pin and follows the case; its questions and answers come along. Its
documents stay in the personal space, so its next questions read the case's documents. Noted in
the case's access log.

403.description: The caller may not contribute to the case, or it is closed

404.description: Not the caller's conversation, or an unknown case

409.description: Already in a case

put.description:
Pin or unpin one of the caller's personal conversations (§3). A conversation in a case has no
pin of its own: it follows its case. Personal, so not in any access log.

409.description: In a case: the case is pinned instead

post.description:
Share one of the caller's conversations with its case (decision 12), or stop sharing it.
Its owner only; a shared conversation is read-only for the case's other members. Noted in the
case's access log. A conversation in the personal space can't be shared.

403.description: The case is closed, or the caller may not contribute to it

404.description: Not the caller's conversation, or not in a case

409.description: The case is strictly confidential

get.description:
The stored documents (newest first) in the caller's personal space, or in the case ``case``,
and the caller's uploads there still being processed or failed.

post.description:
Add a document to the caller's personal space, or to the case ``case`` (a contributor's right): a PDF,
Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), Markdown (.md) or CSV file, recognised by its extension and first bytes.
Returns a job immediately; poll ``GET /v1/documents/jobs/{id}`` until it is ``ready`` (or
``needs_review``), then use its ``document_id`` in chat requests.

A .zip archive adds each of those files inside it as a document of its own: the answer is then
``{"archive": name, "jobs": [job, …], "skipped": [{"name", "failure"}, …]}``, a job per document and
the entries left out, each with why as a message of the registry (``failure``: another kind of file, an
archive inside it, encrypted, too large, empty, not what its extension says, or damaged). With nothing readable in it, ``jobs`` is empty. An archive is
one upload against the queue limits, however many documents it holds.

415.description: Not a PDF, Word, Excel, Markdown, CSV or ZIP file

get.description:
Every document the caller may see, newest first, with its ``case_id`` (null: their personal
space): the sidebar's "Documents" (docs/design/chat-ui.md). No jobs: those are per place.

delete.description:
Cancel one of the caller's uploads (docs/design/chat-ui.md §5, the attachment card's ×): one still
waiting is never read; one being read is stopped, its reader with it, before it is stored. One
already being stored finishes. Noted in the case's access log.

409.description: Already read: it is a document, delete that instead

get.description:
State of one of the caller's uploads: queued, processing, ready, needs_review, failed or cancelled;
while processing, how far reading has got (``progress``: step, pages done, pages); when failed, why
(``error``, in English, for developers, and ``failure``: a code of the registry's ``document`` area with its numbers,
which the interface words in its language).

delete.description:
Delete a document and its passages: one of the caller's own, or one in the case ``case``
(its manager's right). See ``Store.delete_document`` for what deletion does and doesn't guarantee.

Saved conversations that cite it (suveryn-tracker#12): with ``conversations=clean`` (the default)
its passages are taken out of them; with ``conversations=delete`` those conversations are deleted.

202.description: Deleted; the conversations that cite it are cleaned by the next sweep

503.description: Saved conversations can't be reached: nothing was deleted

get.description:
What rebuilds a document sūveryn made (a saved answer's Word file, built in the browser): for
whoever may read it.

404.description: Not here, or nothing to rebuild

get.description:
The saved conversations that cite or attach this document (asked before deleting it): the
caller's own, or in the case ``case`` (its manager, who may delete there) everyone's.

The file a document was read from, as uploaded (board G11, "Open document at p. 3"): for whoever may read
its passages, and noted in the case's access log. A PDF opens in the browser (the page follows as
``#page=3``), Markdown and CSV show as plain text, Word and Excel are downloaded. Text sūveryn stored
itself (a saved answer, a playbook's summary) has none (404).

404.description: Not here, or not an upload

post.description:
Use an upload that carries sūveryn's own export mark as a source anyway (docs/design/chat-ui.md
§6): the person decides, the system only said what it
noticed. The uploader's right in their personal space, a contributor's in a case (as uploading);
in a case the decision goes to its access log. Idempotent.

404.description: Not here, or nothing was noticed

delete.description: Remove the caller's picture; their initials are shown again.

put.description:
Set the caller's picture: the request body is the image (PNG, JPEG or WebP; the UI sends the
square it cropped). It is re-encoded on the server (``avatars.normalise``); answers ``{"avatar": etag}``.

get.description:
The models installed on this appliance, which one is the default, and which is loaded now.

Choosing a model that isn't loaded makes the next answer wait while it loads (seconds when
it was used recently, up to about half a minute otherwise), and other people's questions
wait too: the GPU holds one model at a time.
The live run per case the caller may read, keyed by case id: the chip on the case lists.

The caller's own token usage between ``start`` and ``end`` (ISO 8601 with a time zone;
default: the last 24 hours): totals, a series of buckets in local time, per kind. Never a colleague's.

The office's people (id, username, name) whose username, name or email contains ``q``,
to add a colleague to a case. From Keycloak, through the ``suveryn-directory`` client.

The names of accounts an administrator deleted, by id: what they did in the cases keeps their name
(who added a document, whose shared conversation). Names only.

delete.description: Administrators: remove someone's picture (one that shouldn't be there). Never set one.

get.description:
A colleague's picture (every signed-in user may see it), with an ETag: a browser that has it
sends ``If-None-Match`` and gets 304. 404 when the person has none (the UI shows initials).
